title: Enterprise Onboarding, Integration, Escalation & QBR Playbook
author: Sofia Patel
summary: Consolidated playbook for enterprise onboarding, integration steps, escalation procedures, known issues and workarounds, and QBR/health check templates for high-touch customers.
content:
Overview:

This playbook provides a single reference for Customer Success (CS), Solutions Engineering, and Support teams running enterprise onboarding with Redwood Inference. It covers pre-onboarding prerequisites, a step-by-step integration checklist, escalation paths and SLAs, routine health checks and QBR artifacts, and a curated list of known issues with recommended workarounds. Use this document during onboarding engagements and as the canonical guide for operational escalation and quarterly reviews.

Scope:
- Applies to all enterprise customers onboarding to Redwood Hosted API, Dedicated, or Private deployments.
- Intended audience: CSMs, SEs, Support engineers (L2/L3), SRE oncall, and customer engineering teams.
- Excludes billing disputes and legal contract negotiations (route to Finance/Legal).

Roles & Responsibilities:
- Customer Success Manager (CSM): overall program owner, QBR scheduling, customer adoption metrics.
- Solutions Engineer (SE): integration technical lead, runbook handover, initial performance tuning.
- Support (L2): first escalation point for incidents; triage and reproduce.
- SRE / Runtime Team (L3): ownership of runtime incidents, capacity issues, and kernel-level bugs.
- Account Executive (AE): commercial contract follow-ups and renewals.

Pre-Onboarding checklist (must be completed before technical kickoff):
1. Contract and SOW signed + payment method verified.
2. Customer account created in Redwood Console; provisioned roles and RBAC assigned.
3. Network connectivity validated (for Private/VPC): firewall rules, peering, DNS entries.
4. Exported sample dataset and PII review completed (security sign-off where required).
5. Define success criteria and KPIs: latency SLOs, throughput targets, error budget thresholds.
6. Kickoff scheduled with attendee list (CSM, SE, Customer Eng, Security).

Technical Integration Guide (high-level steps):
- Step 1 \u2014 Environment Preparation:
  - If using Hosted: create API key, whitelist customer origins, and configure rate limits.
  - If using Dedicated/Private: verify VPN/VPC connectivity, KMS integration, and service account creation.
- Step 2 \u2014 Model Selection & Baseline Testing:
  - Run provided perf-bench (curl/CLI) against the selected model for target sequence lengths.
  - Record baseline metrics: p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, error rates.
- Step 3 \u2014 Authentication & Secrets:
  - Configure API keys or mTLS certs. For Private, ensure KMS/HSM keys are attached and rotation policy is scheduled.
- Step 4 \u2014 Prompts, Batching & Caching:
  - Validate prompt templates, enable prefix caching if applicable, and tune batching settings per expected QPS.
- Step 5 \u2014 Observability and Alerts:
  - Enable per-route tracing, token-level cost export, and set alerts for latency (> p95 threshold) and error rate (>1%).
- Step 6 \u2014 Smoke Tests & Handover:
  - Execute smoke tests (generation, chat, embeddings) and hand over runbooks to customer ops team.

Integration Configuration Table (example settings):
| Setting | Recommended Value | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Target p95 latency | "< 500 ms" | For short-text generate workloads (<=512 tokens) on Dedicated; adjust for long contexts. |
| Error rate alert | ">= 1% over 5m" | Triggers L2 triage. |
| Autoscaling policy | "min 2 / max 10 GPU nodes" | Depends on commit and workload spikes. |
| Key rotation | "90 days" | Apply KMS rotation for Private deployments. |

Escalation Playbook (steps & contacts):
1. Triage (Support L2):
   - Gather: customer id, route/model, request id, p95/p99 latency, error logs, and recent deploys.
   - Commands: collect traces (rdwctl trace <request_id>), grab logs from log-export (last 30m).
   - If reproducible and workspace-level: resolve with patch or config change.
2. Rapid Escalation (Support -> SE / CSM):
   - If incident impacts SLA (latency > SLO for >5m, or sustained error rate >5%), notify SE and CSM and create an incident ticket (IMPACT: P2 or P1).
3. Engineering Escalation (SE -> SRE / Runtime Team):
   - Provide perf profiles, kernel traces, and GPU utilization metrics. SRE takes ownership for mitigation steps (hotfix, rollback, capacity increase).
4. Customer Communication:
   - CSM owns customer-facing updates every 30 minutes for P1 and 60 minutes for P2 until remediation.
5. Post-incident:
   - Run RCA and submit a postmortem linked to the incident. Implement remediation and follow-up action items in the next QBR.

Escalation Contacts (roles, not personal emails):
- Support L2 oncall (primary): support-oncall@redwood.ai
- SE escalation channel: #se-escalations (Slack)
- SRE runtime oncall: runtime-oncall@redwood.ai
- CSM escalation: csm-escals@redwood.ai

SLA & Support Tiers (summary):
- Standard (included): 24x5 email support, 48-hour initial response for P3/P4, 8-hour for P2, 4-hour for P1 (business hours).
- Enterprise (paid): 24x7 support, phone escalation, 1-hour initial response for P1, 4-hour for P2.
- Dedicated/Private customers typically qualify for Enterprise tier per contract.

Health Checks & QBR Template:
Cadence:
- Weekly: automated adoption health report (token consumption, route latency, errors) shared with CSM and AE.
- Monthly: Health sync with customer engineering (open issues, planned deployments, roadmap alignment).
- Quarterly: QBR (customer-facing) including exec summary, metrics, actions.

QBR Template (sections):
1. Executive Summary (1 page): adoption, value delivered, renewal risk.
2. Metrics Dashboard: tokens consumed, top routes, p50/p95 latency trends, error rates, cost-per-1k tokens.
3. Reliability Review: incidents since last QBR, RCA status, mitigations.
4. Performance & Cost Optimization: batching, quantization recommendations, and expected savings.
5. Roadmap & Next Steps: features, model upgrades, training sessions.
6. Action Items & Owners: table of actionable follow-ups with owners and due dates.

Known Issues & Workarounds (curated list):
- Issue: Intermittent p95 latency spikes when sequence length > 2048.
  - Severity: High for low-latency apps.
  - Workaround: Provision dedicated longer-context model instance or enable dynamic kernel selection and reduce max_batch_size to prioritize latency.
  - Owner: Runtime team.
- Issue: API rate-limited errors after sustained burst traffic despite autoscale enabled.
  - Severity: Medium
  - Workaround: Increase burst capacity setting, pre-warm additional nodes, and request temporary quota increase via support.
  - Owner: Capacity planning / SRE.
- Issue: Embeddings drift for long-tail tokens after model upgrade.
  - Severity: Low
  - Workaround: Pin previous model for critical routes and run an evaluation testset to validate upgrade before roll-out.
  - Owner: Applied ML / Model Onboarding.

Operational Playbook Snippets (commands & checks):
- Perf bench run: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/perf-bench -H 'Authorization: Bearer <KEY>' -d '{"model":"redwood-1","seq_len":512,"qps":50}'
- Collect runtime snapshot: rdwctl snapshot --route <route> --since 15m --output /tmp/snap.json
- Cost analysis export: Console -> Billing -> Exports -> Last 30 days (csv)

Handover & Success Criteria (example):
- Handover completed when: all smoke tests pass, runbook delivered to customer ops, SLO alerts configured, and an adoption plan with milestones is accepted by customer (signed acceptance email).
- Acceptance KPI examples: 99% of requests under target p95 latency for 14 days; >80% of planned routes receiving production traffic; no P1 incidents in first 30 days.

Postmortem & Continuous Improvement:
- For any Sev1/Sev2 incident, the owning team must publish a postmortem within 7 business days. Postmortems must include timeline, root cause, impact, and remediation. Action items must be tracked in JIRA and reviewed in the following QBR.
